Theme 042 · Metaphor concepts

Security Belt Scan

Every release rides a top-down conveyor through a scanner arch. Inside the arch the frame flips to false-colour X-ray: teal for healthy structure, coral for the thing that should not be there. One package is pushed onto the inspection tray for a human; the belt never stops.

readability ●●●trust ●●○effort med
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

Dashboard tiles tumble onto the belt from the left and pile up while it scrolls right at a steady linear pace. The amber "0 SCANNED" counter blinks on each downbeat of bar 4, just before the drop.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

The camera cranes down onto the arch roof; the lead curtain flaps swing as the belt restarts. On the drop the teal spill blooms outward, the mark and "Acme Pulse" light, and the status LEDs tick on one per 16th note.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

Packages glide left to right; as each crosses the arch a clip-path wipe flips it to X-ray. #2231 lights coral, the pusher arm snaps it down onto the tray on a downbeat (back.out), the monitor punches in, and the human hits "Roll back" while the belt keeps rolling above.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

The camera tilts up off the belt, which keeps scrolling below as a metronome. The tagline slams in word by word on quarter notes; teal ticks pop onto each passing package on the last bar and the coral button lands on the final downbeat.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Belt & rollers — repeating slat pattern that scrolls; the film's only linear motion and its metronome.
  • Scanner arch — roof panel with lead-flap curtain, status LEDs and the lit Acme lockup.
  • X-ray window — false-colour view: teal for healthy structure, coral glow for the anomaly.
  • Detection box — dashed coral bounding box around the suspect layer.
  • Divert arm & tray — pushes one package off the belt to a human; the rest pass.
  • Inspection monitor — enlarged X-ray plus anomaly readout and the Roll back / Acknowledge buttons.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Belt scroll — constant linear translateX, one slat (44 px) per 8th note at 120 BPM; never eases, never stops.
  • Scan wipe — clip-path inset reveals the X-ray view as each package crosses the arch, 0.4 s per item, landing on beats.
  • Divert push — pusher arm rotates 26° with back.out(1.6) in 0.3 s on a snare hit; the monitor punches in 0.95→1 on the next beat.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

A conveyor is the clearest picture of "high volume, checked continuously", and false-colour X-ray makes the invisible problem literally visible. Risk: security and suspicion overtones; scan objects only, never people, and keep the palette calm.

Adapt to your product: Swap the packages for whatever your product processes (pull requests, invoices, orders, uploads) and put your own check result inside the X-ray window.

References: Hugh Turvey, X-ray art · Baggage-scanner colour logic
